overview: The two broad categories of movement across a cell membrane, distinguished by whether cellular energy is spent.
genZNote: Passive transport coasts downhill. Active transport pays the toll to go uphill.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Movement of substances across a membrane against their concentration gradient, requiring energy input (usually ATP).
aspects.valueB: Movement of substances across a membrane down their concentration gradient, requiring no cellular energy.

aspects.label: Energy Requirement
aspects.valueA: Requires ATP (primary active transport) or an existing ion gradient (secondary active transport).
aspects.valueB: No energy input required — driven entirely by the concentration gradient.

aspects.label: Direction of Movement
aspects.valueA: Against the concentration gradient (low to high).
aspects.valueB: Down the concentration gradient (high to low).

aspects.label: Examples
aspects.valueA: Na+/K+ ATPase pump, proton pumps, secondary transporters (symporters/antiporters).

aspects.label: Carrier Involvement
aspects.valueA: Always involves a membrane transport protein (pump).
aspects.valueB: May or may not involve a protein — simple diffusion needs none, facilitated diffusion uses channels/carriers.

aspects.label: Biological Context
aspects.valueA: Maintains ion gradients essential for nerve impulses, nutrient uptake against a gradient, and cell volume regulation.
aspects.valueB: Allows rapid equilibration of gases, small nonpolar molecules, and water across membranes.
